state:
To the Appeals Department, Member ID HMO-4471902, claim reference CLM-MD-88031.

I am writing to appeal the denial of payment for the MRI of my lumbar spine performed on August 29 at Lakeside Imaging. The denial letter says the claim was denied because 'prior authorization was not obtained'. I want to explain what happened, because I believe I did everything I was supposed to do.

My primary care doctor, Dr. Hanna Weiss, ordered the MRI on August 12 after six weeks of physical therapy did not improve my sciatica. Her office told me that they would submit the authorization request, and on August 20 I received an automated text from your plan that said 'Your request has been received and is under review'. I did not receive anything after that. The imaging center called me on August 27 to confirm the appointment and told me that 'everything looks good on the insurance side'. I trusted that, and went ahead with the scan.

I understand now that 'received' does not mean 'approved', but I had no way of knowing that the request was still pending, and neither the doctor's office nor the imaging center told me. The MRI showed a herniated disc at L4-L5, and I am now scheduled to see a spine specialist. I have attached the text message screenshot, the physical therapy discharge summary, and the MRI report.

I am asking that you review the authorization request that was already on file, apply the medical necessity criteria as if it had been completed before the scan, and pay the claim. I am also asking whether the imaging center should have confirmed the authorization before scheduling me, because I am now being billed $1,940.

Thank you for your time.
L. Moreau

The park has a sign at the entrance saying all dogs must be under voice control. There were a few other people around but I don't know any of them and nobody stuck around afterwards. Juniper is up to date on all her vaccines and has never been in a fight before. Do I need to report this to animal control? And will you go after the other owner for the money, or do I have to?
